# Charter — S08 Governance, Modelling, Render and Export (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

- **Project:** S08 'Governance, modelling, render and export', track v1, ADM phase G, delivery plateau, tranche 5, project `01a1d039-0d2c-7bad-8e6c-b5c5d1fd40e2`, plan `docs/plans/slices/S08-governance-modelling.md`. At the 2026-11-27 rework snapshot the project row is `status: closed`, version 8, with `meta.track: v1`, `meta.tranche: 5`, `meta.viability: rework`, `meta.measured_status: built`, `meta.plan_status: planned`, `meta.expected_outputs: [project-brief, evidence]` and no `closure_outputs`. No issue is linked. This rework is retrospective: it reconstructs the lifecycle record from the snapshot and the measured build record, and does not attest contemporaneous intent.
- **Mandate:** deliver the governance and modelling surface the programme needs — portfolio registers, stakeholders, capabilities, deliverables and TOC actions over S03's spine; one flattened model shape for ArchiMate and UML; one deterministic renderer producing SVG, PNG and PDF from a single parse; an XMI exchange that reports what it cannot carry; and two retention producers so the model tables do not grow without bound.
- **Scope:** Part A's 33 actions over the four tables S08 ships plus S03's programme, governed_asset, catalogue_entry, revision and trace_link, and S07's outline/outline_node; Part B's 35 actions over the seven S08 tables (model, model_element, model_relationship, model_view, view_object, view_connection, model_validation_run), the validation job and the four read-only computations; the two byte routes `GET /api/models/{id}/render` and `GET /api/models/{id}/xmi`; migrations 0008–0010. Out of scope: the UI (S12), model search (S07), project CRUD (S05), principle-conflict verdicts (S07), architecture_containers (dropped), change-set/review/publication splits (dropped), graph layout, OCL/Profile/SysML.
- **Expected outputs:** `project-brief`, `evidence`. **Closure outputs:** `closure-review` set by this rework.
- **Acceptance:** the slice gate of SPEC §8 S8 — golden SVG/PNG/PDF/XMI fixtures, and Part A's round-trip as the governance floor — carried by `acceptance/programme/S08.toml` with 17 checks. The gate binaries are `portfolio_roundtrip`, `model_profile` and `model_render` in `conveyor-api`; `s08_models` and `s08_portfolio` in `conveyor-store`; `golden` and `xmi_roundtrip` in `conveyor-render`; and `prune` in `conveyor-server`.
- **Measured build record:** the plan's §7.2 completion record, filled 2026-11-08, is the source of the capability facts: RM's architecture and UML tables held zero rows, so the profiles were derived from the 61-concept registry, fr's render map and the standard; 30 of 61 ArchiMate concepts and 11 relationship kinds are in profile; 10 of 25 UML kinds are in profile; the n8n requirements operations land as actions, never model kinds. The renderer's determinism was measured across two processes; the golden fixtures are checked-in bytes plus a SHA-256 manifest, not insta snapshots.
- **Tranche and governance:** tranche 5 (`01a1e9e0-fe45-77e0-993a-d571fecc5ec1`) is `state: authorised`, authorised at 2026-11-26T22:54:06Z by review `01a21a10-ecb6-70e7-87d5-daa40f5154ac`. The PI plan `01a216d1-1bb7-7376-905e-38a776f22190`, its objectives `01a216d1-1cbe-7297-bc1e-ee5e29ea82cc`, the cadence `01a216d1-1913-70dd-8f69-c8ad230f2364` and the refinement `01a216d1-1a40-7246-ba5e-254b8c0986fe` govern the planning inputs; the refinement records WSJF 6/8/8/7 for S08. The rework runs under standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`. The only contemporaneous S08 publication is the plan and its measured completion record; the record carried no charter, baseline, contract, review or gate receipt before this run.
- **Closure:** S08 is re-closed through the one gate on the record this run creates. The closure is retrospective and its evidence is the acceptance manifest at a fresh snapshot, not a claim that the 2026-11-08 build was contemporaneously reviewed.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — S08 Governance and Modelling (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

body.assignment: The programme architect (conveyor-e2e) is assigned the S08 slice: the governance surface over S03's spine and the modelling surface over seven new tables, with a deterministic renderer and a profile-scoped XMI exchange. The assignment is recorded retrospectively for the 2026-11-27 rework and is bounded by the S08 slice plan.
body.scope: In scope are the 68 actions, the seven S08 tables, the two retention producers, the two byte routes and the seven Phase A–D artefacts. Out of scope are the UI, model search, project CRUD, principle-conflict verdicts, architecture containers, change-set/review/publication splits, graph layout and OCL/Profile/SysML; each exclusion is named in the slice plan's §3 so a later reader cannot mistake absence for omission.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect owns the slice and the acceptance instrument; the Architecture Board approves the Phase A–D set, the contract and the profile; S03 supplies the spine tables and RLS; S04 supplies the registry and invocation route; S07 supplies the outline and the principles/decisions actions; S12 receives the declared trace/architecture surface; the SRO is accountable for the tranche outcome.
body.acceptance_criteria: The S08 gate is the slice gate of SPEC §8 S8: the Part A round-trip from principle to ADR to TOC to register to deliverable to capability to stakeholder, the TOC cycle refusal, the absence of a duplicate principles/decisions surface, three golden models in SVG/PNG/PDF, the profile's write-time 422, the XMI round-trip, the post-commit validation job, deterministic ids, the two retention producers and the render byte-route parity.
body.retrospective: This Statement of Architecture Work is authored by the 2026-11-27 rework from the slice plan, the measured §7.2 completion record and the record's project row. It records the assignment and the acceptance the build was measured against; it does not claim that a contemporaneous board approved this text on 2026-11-08, and it carries that limitation into the Phase-G review.
body.constraints: The build must not introduce a second model store, must not use the registry as the validation authority, must not call load_system_fonts, must not query JSONB geometry in SQL, must not validate inside the mutation transaction, and must not trust an XMI document: size, depth, duplicate ids and a DOCTYPE are refused. These constraints are the plan's traps and are carried into the contract.

risk.title: The Archi 5.10 XMI round-trip is manual, so interoperability is not continuously proven
risk.body: The slice plan's open question 5 records the ArchiMate XMI flavour as the Open Group 3.2 exchange format and the Archi 5.10 round-trip as a manual check. The automated xmi_roundtrip test proves the canonical multiset, the re-export equality and the unsupported[] reporting for the checked-in fixtures, but it does not run a third-party Archi import. Until a manual Archi round-trip is recorded, the interoperability claim rests on the format subset and the codec's own tests.
risk.response: Run one manual Archi 5.10 import and re-export against the S08 profile, record the document and the observed unsupported constructs, and re-read this risk on that evidence.

decisions: D4 XMI is profile-scoped with stated guarantees

risk.title: The profiles were derived from an empty RM dataset, so consumer fit is argued rather than measured live
risk.body: The §7.2 completion record measured zero rows in RM's architecture and UML tables, so the ArchiMate and UML profiles were derived from the 61-concept registry, fr's render map and the standard rather than from live consumer data. The fit is argued from three consumers and the registry, not measured against a populated RM estate. A future RM import could surface a kind the profile defers; the profile is versioned, so adding a kind is a data change with a ruleset bump only when a rule's meaning changes.
risk.response: If RM's modelling tables become populated, re-run the three-consumer extract and record the kinds actually seen; add an in-profile kind rather than widen the renderer silently.

# Project brief — S08 Governance, Modelling, Render and Export (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

## Outcome

S08 delivers the programme's governance and modelling surface: portfolio registers, stakeholders, capabilities, deliverables and TOC actions over S03's spine; one flattened model shape for ArchiMate and UML; one deterministic renderer producing SVG, PNG and PDF from a single parse; an XMI exchange with stated guarantees; and two retention producers. The outcome the record closes on is the acceptance manifest at a fresh snapshot, not the built status alone.

## Boundary

In scope are the 68 actions, the seven S08 tables, the two retention producers, the two byte routes and the seven Phase A–D artefacts. Out of scope are the UI (S12), model search (S07), project CRUD (S05), principle-conflict verdicts (S07), architecture containers, change-set/review/publication splits, graph layout and OCL/Profile/SysML. The boundary is the slice plan's §3, restated so a later reader can see that the exclusions are deliberate.

## Reuse sources

S08 reuses S03's governed_asset, revision, catalogue_entry, trace_link, programme and project spine with RLS and outbox; S04's ActionSpec registry, invocation route and OpenAPI/MCP projection; and S07's outline/outline_node plus the principles.*/decisions.* actions. It ships no duplicate of those surfaces: the registry dump has no S08-owned principles.* or decisions.*, and the TOC tables stay S07's.

## Inception units

The build units are the slice plan's 21 steps: migrations 0008–0010; the domain and store for portfolio and models; the Part A actions and the TOC actions; the Part A round-trip; the seven model tables; the two profiles; the model, element, relationship, view and connection actions; the renderer in three formats; the XMI codec; the validation job; the four read-only tools; the retention producers; the three exchange actions and two byte routes; the served-spec lock; and the gate.

## Dependencies

S08 depends on S03 (spine, RLS, outbox), S04 (registry, invocation, projection) and S07 (outline, principles/decisions). It is a tranche-5 member and its planning inputs are the PI plan, objectives, cadence and refinement named in the charter. It declares the trace/architecture surface for S12 and the model SSE topic; those are declarations, not builds.

## Acceptance

The acceptance is `acceptance/programme/S08.toml` with 17 checks, backed by the gate binaries `portfolio_roundtrip`, `model_profile` and `model_render` in conveyor-api; `s08_models` and `s08_portfolio` in conveyor-store; `golden` and `xmi_roundtrip` in conveyor-render; and `prune` in conveyor-server. The properties are the plan's a–j: Part A round-trip, TOC legality, no double definition, golden fixtures, profile rejection, XMI round-trip, post-commit validation, id determinism, retention and artefact parity.

## Capabilities

The built capability set is sixfold: portfolio governance (33 actions), TOC planning (10 actions over S07 tables), model authoring (32 actions over seven tables), validation and analysis (5 read actions), render and exchange (3 actions plus 2 byte routes) and retention (2 job kinds). The two profiles are conveyor-archimate-3.2-v1 (30 + 11) and conveyor-uml-2.5.1-v1 (10 + 9 plus 5 diagram kinds), frozen on 2026-11-08.

## Plan

The plan is the slice plan's 21-step build order, completed and measured on 2026-11-08. This rework does not rebuild it: it supplies the lifecycle record the build did not leave behind, re-runs the acceptance at a fresh snapshot and closes on that receipt. The remaining work is the manual Archi 5.10 XMI round-trip and a re-read of the profile if RM's modelling tables become populated.

# Architecture Artefact Index — S08 (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

## Metadata

The artefact set for S08 is the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts on the delivery track: the Stakeholder Map, Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog, Requirements Catalog and Solution Concept Diagram at phase A on the preliminary-statement plateau; the Business Capability Map at phase B on the high-level-design plateau; the Data Entity/Data Component Catalog at phase C; and the Technology Standards Catalog at phase D. All seven are authored under the 2026-11-27 retrospective rework for project 01a1d039-0d2c-7bad-8e6c-b5c5d1fd40e2, tranche 5, under standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14.

## Entries

The index names each artefact and its role: the stakeholder map fixes who decides and who is consulted; the driver/goal catalogue fixes the six decisions and five goals that bound the profile; the requirements catalogue carries eight executable requirements; the solution concept shows the author-publish-render-exchange path; the capability map records six built capabilities; the data catalogue records the seven S08 tables and four reused S03 tables; the technology catalogue names the two profiles, the renderer versions, the XMI scope and the vendored fonts.

## Links

Each artefact links to another artefact of this pack, so the set has no orphan: the stakeholder map depends on the capability map, the driver catalogue derives the requirements catalogue, the requirements realise the solution concept, and the capability, data and technology catalogues form the dependency chain back to the stakeholder map. These are the same edges the factory writes through architecture.artifacts_link.

## Document

This index is itself an architecture-artifact document, composed and published in the architecture-artifact category. It carries the retrospective provenance: the S08 product was measured complete on 2026-11-08 in the slice plan's §7.2 record; the record carried no lifecycle set; this rework authored the seven artefacts, the charter, the Statement of Architecture Work, the delivery contract and the Phase-G review so the project can close on evidence rather than on a status claim. The index does not attest contemporaneous intent.

# Closure review — S08 Governance, Modelling and Render (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

## Outcome vs acceptance

The outcome the charter records is the governance and modelling surface — 68 actions, seven S08 tables, a deterministic renderer and a profile-scoped XMI exchange — and the acceptance the record carries is `acceptance/programme/S08.toml`: 17 checks plus the gate, green at the fresh 2026-11-27 snapshot. Against that acceptance the historical record was closed on the built status alone, with no charter, baseline, contract, review or gate receipt; this review records both states honestly.

## Evidence

The evidence is the seven Phase A–D artefacts and their index, the charter, the Statement of Architecture Work, the delivery contract, the approved scope baseline, the compliant Phase-G review, the closure gate and the fresh receipt. The product evidence is the slice plan's §7.2 completion record of 2026-11-08 (migrations 0008–0010, 68 actions, the two profiles, the golden bytes and the XMI round-trip fixtures) and the gate binaries the plan's §7 names. The evidence is retrospective: it reconstructs the lifecycle and does not attest contemporaneous approval.

## Open items

Two items remain open and are named rather than rounded up. First, the Archi 5.10 XMI round-trip is a manual check: the automated codec tests prove the canonical multiset and the unsupported[] reporting, but no third-party Archi import is recorded. Second, the profiles were derived from an empty RM modelling dataset, so consumer fit is argued from the registry, fr's render map and the standard; if RM's tables become populated, the three-consumer extract must be re-run. Neither item blocks the close; both are registers S08-R1 and S08-R2.

## Decision

The decision is to close S08 on the record set this run creates. The closure gate is approved by an approver distinct from its requester; the destructive close gate names the closure asset as its typed evidence; and the whole run is recorded under standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`. The close is retrospective, the two open items stay managed, and any later contemporaneous record must be read against this review rather than silently overwrite it.
